title: Define verified-session handoff and rollover

requirement.summary: Prevent a verified task from owning agentgov next forever after Monitor while preserving immutable evidence and explicit human meaning.

objective.rationale: The guided loop needs an explicit non-approval terminal transition before it can route another task or later consider update availability.

goal: Specify a fresh-verified, explicitly confirmed, append-only session handoff and a deterministic rollover route that keeps the active pointer and task artifacts intact.
non_goals: Do not implement govern handoff, add or change an event type, change the session or Monitor schema, alter next routing, or modify CLI arguments in this decision slice.
Do not delete, archive, rename, or rewrite .agentgov/current-task.json, existing events, task contracts, completion evidence, or Monitor output.
Do not equate Monitor generation, handoff, or rollover with requirement correctness, architecture approval, merge readiness, task deletion, or human acceptance of the implementation.
Do not add Monitor self-reporting, hidden acknowledgement state, hooks, daemons, background checks, update routing, exception records, or telemetry.
Do not commit in the AgentGov source repository, push, tag, publish, release, migrate a consumer, change a workflow, merge, deploy, or mutate an external system.
Preserve all earlier uncommitted bounded slices and report their combined working-copy scope honestly.
acceptance_signals: The decision chooses one explicit session.handed_off event rather than deleting the current-task pointer, mutating the task decision, or making Monitor generation a hidden state transition.

Handoff is admissible only for the exact active task digest and base after the latest completion is verified and still fresh; drift, stale evidence, failed scope, invalid events, or an unverified completion blocks it.

A future govern handoff command must preview one append-only event target and require exact HANDOFF confirmation from a real terminal; dry-run, redirected, cancelled, and non-interactive paths write nothing.
The handoff event records that a human ended routing responsibility for one working-copy session, not that requirements, architecture, implementation, or Monitor content were approved.
The current-task pointer, task contract, evidence, and prior events remain intact; repeated handoff is idempotent and does not append duplicates.
After handoff, next may recommend a new or explicitly selected task through govern start --replace-active --dry-run and must not automatically rediscover the same handed-off task digest.
Multiple remaining tasks still require explicit human choice, while a changed digest may be considered a new reviewed task version only through normal start confirmation.
Monitor remains a derived read model; a future successful Monitor command may print the handoff preview as its next command but cannot assert that a human read or approved the output.
Current runtime, schema, CLI, event, Monitor, next, release, workflow, and update behavior remains unchanged in this decision slice.
Documentation tests protect the event-only atomic boundary, freshness gate, no-approval semantics, pointer preservation, idempotence, and rollover choice rules.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_user_documentation tests.test_next_action tests.test_development_session tests.test_event_store tests.test_development_monitor -v

items: Deleting the pointer could lose session identity or make the same completed task look new.
A handoff event could be mistaken for semantic approval or Monitor review if its authority boundary is vague.
A pointer-plus-event transition could become non-atomic if implementation writes more than the append-only event.
Task discovery could restart a handed-off digest or silently choose among several remaining tasks.

stop_conditions: Stop if safe handoff requires deleting or rewriting the active pointer, prior events, task artifacts, or completion evidence.
Stop if freshness cannot be re-established from the exact verified evidence before confirmation.
Stop if the event meaning would imply requirement correctness, architecture approval, merge readiness, or proof that Monitor was reviewed.
Stop if rollover must guess human task choice or restart the same handed-off digest automatically.
Stop if the decision requires runtime, schema, workflow, release, consumer, or external-state mutation.

decision.rationale: The user explicitly asked to continue with the next recommended verified-session handoff and rollover contract. The delivered task was paused on 2026-08-05 to remove it from automatic discovery; this is routing hygiene, not a claim of semantic completion, acceptance, merge, or release.
